cards.power: (The Skeptic's Lens): Demands every Theory-Wrestler prove themselves through repeatable experiments, not elegant words.
cards.lore: The Father of the Scientific Method. He moved science from Philosophical-Guessing to Empirical-Testing.
cards.gradeReason: Historical icon needs context to fully inhabit — the empiricist stance is there but buried.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grunge science zine. Subject: Owl scholar with magnifying glass demanding proof. Mood: Stern curiosity.

cards.power: (The Jugna-Ganasher): Physically shows that the Old-Scrolls are wrong by looking at the Real-Wrestler-Body.
cards.lore: Champions the Troupe tradition. If the book says one thing and the body shows another, trust the body.
cards.gradeReason: Clear dissector role but requires knowing Vesalius's historical rebellion to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grunge anatomy illustration. Subject: Ape anatomist exposing skeleton, book discarded. Mood: Revolutionary clarity.

cards.power: (The Fragile-Signal): Identifies the Invisible-Enemy before the arena is ready to believe it, suffering professional exile.
cards.lore: The cost of being right too early. Evidence is often rejected by the Consensus-Board if it challenges professional status.
cards.gradeReason: Tragic outsider hero is instantly embodiable — you ARE the ignored whistleblower.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark zine tragedy. Subject: Raccoon outsider with data scrolls, rejected by crowd. Mood: Defiant and doomed.

cards.power: (The Micro-Defense): Proves that Invisible-Invaders cause the Arena-Collapse, providing the first systematic Shilds.
cards.lore: Changed the Cosmic Biology to the Invader-Logic. Turned Miasma-Mystery into Pathogen-Logic.
cards.gradeReason: Clear germ-theory champion but the vaccine framing needs table context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian science punk. Subject: Badger alchemist with glowing vials defeating green monster. Mood: Triumphant precision.

cards.power: (The Black Swan-Strikes): Declares a Theory-Wrestler is only scientific if there is a more that can kill it.
cards.lore: Science doesn't Prove truths, it Disproves falsehood. A theory stays in the ring only until falsified.
cards.gradeReason: Kill-the-theory demand is immediately performable — every player becomes an attack dog.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Wrestling zine noir. Subject: Rhino philosopher smashing a glass sphere with black swan inside. Mood: Relentless challenge.

cards.power: (The Arena-Reset): Shows science moves in sudden Paradigm-Collapses where old rules are deleted.
cards.lore: Normal science works within a box until Anomalies pile up, leading to a Scientific-Riot (a.k.a. Paradigm Shift).
cards.gradeReason: Paradigm-flip role is instantly embodied — you blow up the whole ring and start fresh.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grunge disruption explosion. Subject: Gorilla wrestler flipping a wrestling ring mid-match. Mood: Chaotic transformation.

cards.power: (The Efficiency-Cut): Slices through complex, bloated Conspiracy-Theories to reveal the simplest path fitting the Star-Data.
cards.lore: Entities should not be multiplied without necessity.
cards.gradeReason: Cut to simplest explanation — zero ambiguity, pure performative slash.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Clean precision zine. Subject: Praying mantis slicing through tangled theory webs. Mood: Elegant minimalism.

cards.power: (The Dogma-Trap): Wears the mask of Science but behaves like a Religion.
cards.lore: The corruption of the Scientific Method when Science becomes Dogma. Forgetting to Ask Questions. Forgetting is the Process of Questioning.
cards.gradeReason: False-prophet villain is immediately inhabited — the preach-without-evidence character is crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark satire zine. Subject: Sheep in lab coat preaching from altar, true believers below. Mood: Sinister sanctimony.

cards.power: (The Max-Shield): Exposes the Chemical-Ally wins because it's actually strong, not because the coach believed it.
cards.lore: Randomization and Blinding. The only way to defeat Placebo-the-Trickster.
cards.gradeReason: Gold Standard role clear for med players, but needs table context for civilians.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Clinical champion zine. Subject: Armored elephant with double-blind shield blocking placebo ghost. Mood: Methodological authority.

cards.power: (The Fluke-Filter): Tells you if the Match-Outcome was a Real-Skill Win or a Random-Dice-Roll.
cards.lore: Probability of observing results if the Null is true. Corrupt. Easily tricked by P-Hacking-the-Cheat.
cards.gradeReason: The fluke-filter role is clear but p-value mechanics require some statistical literacy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Neon probability zine. Subject: Monkey juggling coins and dice above significance threshold line. Mood: Unreliable authority.

cards.power: (The Status-Bar-Guard): Assumes the new Drug-Wrestler is useless until proven otherwise with Overwhelming Evidence.
cards.lore: The conservative heart of science. You don't win until you KO-the-Ghost.
cards.gradeReason: Bored skeptic who assumes nothing works — instantly playable, delightfully obstructionist.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pale ghost zine comedy. Subject: Drowsy seal ghost blocking ring entry, arms crossed. Mood: Aggressively indifferent.

cards.power: (The Arena-Synthesis): Gathers All different Match-Tapes and combines them into one Giant Verdict.
cards.lore: Pooling data to increase power. Identifies the True-Signal buried in the Noise of smaller matches.
cards.gradeReason: Aggregator role is clear but the forest-plot synthesis needs statistical context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Archival giant zine. Subject: Spider weaving multiple match films into one glowing web verdict. Mood: Supreme synthesis.

cards.power: (The Funding-Friction): Decides which Wrestlers get into the arena based on Profit-Potential rather than Cure-Potential.
cards.lore: Research follows the money. Creates Incentive-Glitches treating only profitable symptoms.
cards.gradeReason: Profit-over-cure villain is instantly inhabited — the villain pose is zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corrupt capitalist zine. Subject: Lizard in suit blocking ring with money bags, denying entry. Mood: Smug obstruction.

cards.power: (The Statistic-Torture): Tortures the Data-Wrestler until it Confesses to a significant result, even if there isn't one.
cards.lore: Running 100 tests until one looks Significant by chance. Turns Noise into False-Verdicts.
cards.gradeReason: The torturous data-cheat is immediately performable — everyone knows this villain from experience.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark data crime zine. Subject: Ferret in interrogation room forcing data to confess under lamplight. Mood: Gleeful corruption.

cards.power: (The File-Drawer Trap): Hides every Losing-Match-Tape in a basement creating the Illusion of 100% win ratio.
cards.lore: The Filter of Success. It skews Meta-Analysis because the Evidence-Pile is missing all failures.
cards.gradeReason: The file-drawer villain is immediately playable — destroy the loser tapes, show only wins.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Archive conspiracy zine. Subject: Walrus hiding stacks of negative results in basement vault. Mood: Smugly selective.

cards.power: (The Hidden Influence): Whispers to the Principal Investigator, Interpreting a Tie-Match as a Victory for the Sponsor.
cards.lore: Financial ties compromise objectivity. Interpreting Tie-Matches as sponsor victories.
cards.gradeReason: Shadowy whisperer role is clear — slightly more theatrical than immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark conspiracy zine. Subject: Chameleon scientist whispering in researcher's ear while sponsor money bag lurks. Mood: Insidious subtle.

cards.power: (The In-Silico-Sprint): Runs a billion Virtual-Matches in a second to find the perfect Protein-Amino-Shape before a real lab opens.
cards.lore: Machine learning in drug discovery. Finds patterns the human brain could never see.
cards.gradeReason: Billion-match sprinter is vivid but performing AI omniscience needs table framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Neon neural network zine. Subject: Octopus brain scanning millions of molecular matches simultaneously. Mood: Superhuman velocity.

cards.power: (The Individual-Verdict): Tailors the Chemical-Ally to fit your specific DNA-Lock.
cards.lore: Moving from Population-Average to Individual-Reality. The Standard-Mean is replaced by the Personal-Match.
cards.gradeReason: DNA-lock sniper is vivid but the one-of-one premise requires genetic literacy to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Precision sci-fi zine. Subject: Cat sniper with DNA helix scope targeting specific gene lock. Mood: Surgical individualism.

cards.power: (The Information-Burst): Bypasses the Peer-Review-Pandemonium to deliver Match-Results instantly.
cards.lore: Rapid dissemination vs Rigor. Great for Pandemic-Panic, but prone to Error-Glitches.
cards.gradeReason: Speed-bypass role is clear but the double-edged-sword tension needs context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Racing speedrunner zine. Subject: Cheetah sprinting past peer-review gate with unverified scroll. Mood: Reckless velocity.

cards.power: (The Paywall-Breaker): Smashes the Journal-Fortress gates so every Roster-Doctor can see the Research-Bundle.
cards.lore: The movement for Democratic-Data. If the public paid for the match, they should see the tape for free.
cards.gradeReason: Gate-smashing knight is vivid but the paywall politics need context to fully embody the rage.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Liberation crusade zine. Subject: Rhino knight in armor smashing journal paywall fortress gate. Mood: Democratic fury.

cards.power: (The Uncertainty-Bracket): Shows the True-Value must-Almost-Ever if the arena is too wide, the Verdict is a shaky guess.
cards.lore: Tells you where the True-Value is. The narrower the bracket, the more precise the move.
cards.gradeReason: Pure stats bracket — describes the concept precisely but invites no embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Statistical precision zine. Subject: Wizard holding glowing bracket with narrow confidence beam. Mood: Cautious precision.

cards.power: (The Connection-Strength): Tells you how much of the Outcome is actually explained by the Variable-Move.
cards.lore: Correlation vs Causation. If R-Square is low, the connection is Noise and the Theory is weak.
cards.gradeReason: Explanation-power role is clear — you measure how much you actually matter. Playable but stat-adjacent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Data math zine. Subject: Beaver measuring cause-effect bridge with R² coefficient gauge. Mood: Analytical doubt.

cards.power: (The Reality-Check): Tells you how many Wrestlers you must treat to save one from a Lethal-Outcome.
cards.lore: Translates Complex-Research-Math into Bedside-Reality. An NNT of 1000 is a weak move.
cards.gradeReason: A stat translation card — informative, grounded, but performs nothing at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Clinical reality zine. Subject: Saint Bernard counting 1000 wrestlers to save one trophy. Mood: Sobering arithmetic.

cards.power: (The Speed-of-Death): Tells you if the Chemical-Ally slows down the Clock-of-Disease compared to the Placebo-Ghost.
cards.lore: Used in Oncology. Compares Event-Rate between two groups throughout the whole match.
cards.gradeReason: Survival-analysis stat — pure measurement tool, no embodiment invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Oncology thriller zine. Subject: Rabbit racing clock against cancer demon with hourglass stopwatch. Mood: Urgent calculation.

cards.power: (The History-Appeals): Finds wrestlers who already lost, looking back to see if they touched the same Toxic-Shield.
cards.lore: Outcome back to Exposure. Best for Rare-Zebra hunts where you can't wait for a new study.
cards.gradeReason: Time-rewind detective role is vivid — backward-in-time investigator needs design context to fully click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Noir detective zine. Subject: Dog detective with magnifier examining old match tapes and toxic shields. Mood: Retrospective pursuit.

cards.power: (The Long-Match): Takes a group of Exposure-Wrestlers and follows them for 20 years to see who Crashes first.
cards.lore: Exposure forward to Outcome. The Gold Standard of observational matches.
cards.gradeReason: Patient 20-year stalker role is clear — the long-game embodiment needs chronological framing at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Prospective safari zine. Subject: Giraffe with binoculars tracking wrestler group across decades on timeline. Mood: Patient surveillance.

cards.power: (The Bias-Eraser): Ensures Expectation-Sparks don't pollute the Data-Stream. Both Wrestler and Ref are in the dark on what quantity.
cards.lore: The ultimate defense against Placebo-the-Trickster and Investigator-Effect Bias.
cards.gradeReason: Blindfold-the-ref stance is immediately performable — blackout justice, no exceptions.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Blindfold justice zine. Subject: Armored badger referee blindfolded holding scales perfectly balanced. Mood: Incorruptible fairness.

cards.power: (The Mind-Healer): Heals the Wrestler just by making them believe they get a better Chemical-Ally in a Clinical trial.
cards.lore: The power of belief. Science must prove its Move is stronger than the Trickster's mojo.
cards.gradeReason: Belief-healer trickster is immediately inhabited — the psychosomatic con artist performs itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Fox magician zine. Subject: Fox in lab coat handing sugar pill with dazzling belief-sparkle effect. Mood: Benevolent deception.

cards.power: (The Human-Shield): Ensures Wrestlers are not treated like Laboratory-Rats and the match is worth the risk.
cards.lore: The response to Historical-Horrors. Research must serve the subject, not just the Data Gods.
cards.gradeReason: Ethical protector stance is admirable and clear — needs historical horror context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ethical guardian zine. Subject: Tortoise in golden armor shielding small creatures from scientist. Mood: Solemn protection.

cards.power: (The Sovereign-Voice): Ensures the Wrestler knows exactly what Monsters are in the arena before entering the ring.
cards.lore: The legal and ethical Shield of Autonomy. Science cannot happen in secret.
cards.gradeReason: Autonomy-scroll role is clear but performs better as context card than character embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Legal scroll zine. Subject: Lemur reading glowing consent document with monsters visible in background arena. Mood: Informed sovereignty.

cards.power: (The Protocol-Police): Reads the Match-Plan before it starts and Blocks any match that is Legally Shaky.
cards.lore: Big cop oversight. Prevents Mad-Scientist-Heel-Turns by demanding ethical accountability.
cards.gradeReason: Bureaucratic gatekeeper is playable but the IRB archetype needs institutional context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bureaucratic gatekeeper zine. Subject: Raccoon in suit raising STOP hand at scientist with suspicious protocol. Mood: Cautious authority.

cards.power: (The Universal-Rulebook): Sets the Global Standard for how Human-Wrestlers must be treated in every arena on Earth.
cards.lore: The ethical Constitution of the World Medical Association.
cards.gradeReason: Global constitution is important but reads as a descriptor, not an invitation to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Global mandate zine. Subject: Golden globe with declaration scroll descending onto all wrestling arenas. Mood: Universal gravitas.

cards.power: (The Infinite-Library): Looks at millions of Electronic-Health-Scrolls to find Hidden-Patterns a tiny-RCT would miss.
cards.lore: The shift from Sampling to Total-Observation. Powerful, but prone to Noise-Glitches.
cards.gradeReason: Omniscient library giant is vivid — the scale of performance is immediately attractive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Data titan zine. Subject: Blue octopus titan holding city of health records, searching for signals. Mood: Overwhelming omniscience.

cards.power: (The Illusion-Mist): Makes it look like Move-A caused Outcome-B, but really it was Variable-C hiding in the shadows.
cards.lore: Correlation is not Causation. The nemesis of Logic-the-Razor.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow-variable illusionist is immediately embodied — you ARE the hidden third cause.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Illusion villain zine. Subject: Wolf emerging from smoke between two fighters who blame each other. Mood: Invisible mischief.

cards.power: (The Public-Vow): Makes the Coach announce the Match-Rules before the fight, preventing them from changing the Winning-Criteria later.
cards.lore: Transparency. Prevents Outcome-Switching and Marking.
cards.gradeReason: Pre-commitment enforcer role is clear — but ClinicalTrials.gov mechanics need context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Transparency enforcement zine. Subject: Rooster announcing match rules to crowd before fight begins. Mood: Preemptive accountability.

cards.power: (The Reality-Check): Demands the Miracle-Victory be performed again in a Different-Arena. If it can't be repeated, it's not a fact.
cards.lore: A single win is a fluke; a repeatable win is a fact.
cards.gradeReason: Do it again, different arena — the replication demand is immediately performable and fun.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Replication challenge zine. Subject: Owl referee demanding second performance in different ring. Mood: Skeptical insistence.

cards.power: (The Isolated-Brawl): Allows the Chemical-Ally to fight the Pathogen-Punk in glass without the Wrestler-Body interfering.
cards.lore: The Initial-Testing-Ground. Cells in a dish don't behave like cells in a human.
cards.gradeReason: Isolation-arena role is clear — lab context helps, but the controlled-glass-arena concept is vivid.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Micro-arena zine. Subject: Tiny wrestlers fighting inside giant glowing petri dish controlled by giant hands. Mood: Contained experiment.

cards.power: (The Proxy-Wrestler): Takes the Chemical-Hits first to see if the Arena-Stats are safe for humans.
cards.lore: The Translational bridge from Dish to Human, though Mice are not small men.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrificial proxy role is clear — the noble/tragic mouse framing works but needs lab context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Translational bridge zine. Subject: Tiny mouse in wrestling gear standing bravely before massive experimental arena. Mood: Noble sacrifice.

cards.power: (The Protein-Scanner): Identifies exactly which Protein-Armor-Pieces are being built by the cell in what quantity.
cards.lore: Molecular biology. The Hardware-Audit of the cell.
cards.gradeReason: SDS-PAGE hardware audit — purely technical lab method, zero embodiment invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Molecular lab zine. Subject: Zebra scientist running gel electrophoresis stripes glowing identification. Mood: Precise quantification.

cards.power: (The Source-Code-Kill): Deletes a single Manual-Page (Gene) to see if the Wrestler can survive without it.
cards.lore: Functional genomics. If the wrestler Crashes, we know the gene's Power-Level.
cards.gradeReason: Delete-one-gene-and-watch is vivid — the crash-test premise is immediately graspable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: CRISPR action zine. Subject: Crab with scissors cutting single page from giant DNA manual, wrestler wobbling. Mood: Precise elimination.

cards.power: (The Lifeline): Provides the Tokens needed to pay the Arena-Fees and bring the Wrestlers to the ring.
cards.lore: Competition for resources. Only the most Resourceful-Grantee makes it. Without him, science stops.
cards.gradeReason: Funding-mechanism card describes a structural role — no performative invitation at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Resource gatekeeper zine. Subject: Pelican in tuxedo dispensing gold coins to waiting scientists. Mood: Competitive scarcity.

cards.power: (The Exclusive-Contract): Ensures only one Coach can call the Chemical-Ally, charging high Fees for Restricted-Access.
cards.lore: The economic engine of drug discovery. Balances Innovation-Incentive vs Access-Cost.
cards.gradeReason: Patent-dragon role is clear — the exclusivity enforcer is playable but structural tension needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dragon monopoly zine. Subject: Green dragon sitting on pile of drug patents blocking access gate. Mood: Possessive exclusivity.

cards.power: (The Critical-Block): Finds every tiny Glitch in the Match-Tape and demands a Rematch (Revision) before the world sees it.
cards.lore: Quality-Control. The most feared Gremlin in the Academia-Arena.
cards.gradeReason: Feared gremlin critic is instantly inhabitable — the nitpick-everything role plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Academic villain zine. Subject: Skunk with red pen circling every flaw in journal manuscript. Mood: Delightfully merciless.

cards.power: (The Prestige-Rank): Decides how much weight the Match-Result carries. The Lancet, Nature, Science, NEJM.
cards.lore: The Currency-of-Prestige. Leads to Bias for High-Rank Journals. Tracks really high-scoring matches only.
cards.gradeReason: Prestige-gatekeeper is clear — performing journal hierarchy needs academic-world context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Prestige hierarchy zine. Subject: Mountain goat climbing journal prestige pyramid with impact score crown at top. Mood: Status obsession.

cards.power: (The Dogma-Defense): Refuses to believe the Consensus-Wrestler until the Raw-Data-Scrolls are shown.
cards.lore: The organized skepticism in the reliability of expert opinion.
cards.gradeReason: Show-me-the-data defense is instantly embodied — zero ambiguity, pure skeptic stance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Skeptic champion zine. Subject: Lion holding NULLIUS IN VERBA shield against wave of authority claims. Mood: Principled defiance.

cards.power: (The False-Connection): Shows two things moving together, but warns that one did NOT cause the other.
cards.lore: The most common Thinking-Trap. Tag team partners aren't necessarily the boss of each other.
cards.gradeReason: Classic science meme as a card — ice cream and drowning penguins walk together. Table-ready instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Spurious zine comedy. Subject: Two penguins in synchronized costumes with broken causation arrow between them. Mood: Playfully misleading.

cards.power: (The Number-Game): Focuses on changing a Stat instead of the Real-Outcome (Death). You win the Stat-Match but lose the Life-Match.
cards.lore: A Better-Number doesn't always mean a Better-Patient.
cards.gradeReason: The stat-vs-outcome tension is real but abstract — hard to perform at table without clinical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Hollow victory zine. Subject: Doctor celebrating HbA1c number while patient still collapses behind them. Mood: Pyrrhic statistical triumph.

cards.power: (The Stress-Tester): Changes the Match-Rules slightly to see if the Verdict still stands. If it breaks, the research was Fragile.
cards.lore: A strong verdict should survive many different Arena-Conditions.
cards.gradeReason: Robustness check describes methodology — performs as QA tool, not embodiable character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Stress test zine. Subject: Gorilla stress-testing bridge under different weather conditions, noting which breaks. Mood: Rigorous probing.

cards.power: (The People's Arena): Bypasses the Academic-Monopoly, allowing thousands of Non-Wrestlers to contribute data.
cards.lore: The democratization of discovery. Patient-Led-Research.
cards.gradeReason: Anti-monopoly crowd role is vivid — but the biohacking premise needs ideological framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grassroots science zine. Subject: Crowd of diverse citizens flooding academic arena with data contributions. Mood: Democratic uprising.

cards.power: (The Wild-Arena-Test): Looks at how the Chemical-Ally performs in the messy real world with Multi-Morb-Mix wrestlers.
cards.lore: Identifies Side-Effect-Saboteurs that only appear once millions are treated.
cards.gradeReason: Post-market surveillance detective is clear — real-world chaos vs trial order is performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Wild arena detective zine. Subject: Trench coat detective tracking drug through chaotic real-world arena crowd. Mood: Messy truth-seeking.

cards.power: (The Truth-Revealer): Demands the Raw-Match-Tapes be available for anyone to Fact-Check.
cards.lore: The cure for P-Hacker-the-Cheat. If you show the work, the Cheat can't hide.
cards.gradeReason: Open-data crusader is clear — the anti-cheat crusade is vivid, needs cheater to really ignite.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Transparency crusade zine. Subject: Armadillo opening all data vaults to sunlight, cheater fleeing. Mood: Radical openness.

cards.power: (The Moral-Brake): Ensures the Human-Wrestler still has the Final-Say and isn't just a Data-Point for the AI.
cards.lore: The challenge of Autonomous Biology. We must ensure the Pattern-Finder is responsible.
cards.gradeReason: Human-override guardian is topical and clear — AI ethics framing needs current context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: AI ethics zine. Subject: Elephant guardian pulling brake lever on runaway AI algorithm train. Mood: Necessary intervention.

cards.power: (The Rigor Enforcer): Trust the method, not the person. Double the consensus until the data is raw.
cards.lore: Science is searching for the truth, not Safety. Stay Fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: The host card is the ultimate performance — FrizzleBob IS the table's skeptic-in-chief.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mascot boss zine. Subject: Rabbit MC in lab coat holding lantern, master of epistemology in chaotic ring. Mood: Chaotic authority.

cards.lore: Big Pharma funds a drug. Results look Significant, but the NNT is 5000. QUEST: Summon Scientism-the-False-God and deploy Replication-Match to demand strict P-Test.
cards.gradeReason: Boss battle with clear combo mechanic — multi-card quest needs setup but the stakes are obvious.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Villain combo boss zine. Subject: Big Pharma frog + P-Hacker ferret shaking hands over falsified data graph. Mood: Corrupt conspiracy.

cards.lore: A massive Signal challenges the consensus. The Peer-Review refuses certification. QUEST: Deploy Open-the-Access-Knight and get the data to the arena!
cards.gradeReason: Censorship boss battle with clear resolution path — the liberation quest is immediately graspable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Censorship siege zine. Subject: Burning manuscript pile with access knight charging journal fortress. Mood: Suppressed revelation.

cards.lore: AI finds a hidden Genetic-Glitch causing Heart-Collapse in low Cardiology-Patients. QUEST: Combine AI-the-Pattern-Predictor + Precision-the-Genetic-Sniper, while ensuring Ethical-the-AI-Limit protects Wrestler-ethics.
cards.gradeReason: Three-card combo boss needs setup but the AI+precision+ethics triumvirate is conceptually tight.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: AI hunt boss zine. Subject: Zebra genome map with AI scan beam finding hidden heart flaw, ethics brake visible. Mood: High-stakes discovery.

verdict: Peer-Review Pandemonium is the most complete educational kayfabe deck in the corpus — 56 cards covering the full lifecycle of science from Alhazen to AI ethics, zero filler. The wrestling metaphors are airtight: P-Hacker-the-Cheat, Null-the-Boring-Ghost, Confound-the-Distractor — these names alone earn the deck. The G2-heavy distribution (54%) is expected for an educational deck; civilian players need context, but med students and science communicators will grade half the deck G1 on instinct. Boss Battle cards on page 15 are a standout mechanic, turning three-card combos into teachable moments. Weak spot: the stat cards (NNT, Hazard Ratio, CI) are G3 descriptors that inform but don't invite. Table-ready YES — especially for medical education, science journalism workshops, and academic satire events.
blurb: 56-card cage match through the entire scientific method — from Alhazen's repeatable experiment to AI's moral brake. For med students, science communicators, and anyone who's wanted to body-slam a p-value.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 13 card pages (4 cards each = 52 regular cards) + 1 boss page (Doc FrizzleBob + 3 Boss Battles = 4 special cards). Total 56 cards. Page 7 labeled 'What the FLUFF?!' (stats section). Page 8 labeled OBSERVATIONAL / INTERVENTIONAL. Page 10 labeled 'The Data-Kayfabe'. Boss Battles on page 15 introduce multi-card combo quest mechanic — unique to this deck. No RAF dice boxes visible. Power/lore text baked into decorative fonts; some cards on pages 7 and 13 had partially obscured text at render resolution. 'Vesali' is the card spelling of Vesalius; 'Semme' is Semmelweis. Thomas Kuhn attribution on page 3 reads 'Thomas Kunn' — possible font artifact or intentional kayfabe spelling.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: THE EPISTEMIA EDGE – Peer-Review Pandemonium & the Science of Not Getting Fooled (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated mnemonic cards to master how real evidence is built, how p-hacking and confounders fake it, and how peer review still waves bad science straight to the bedside.

In 1847 a doctor worked out that physicians were carrying death from the autopsy table to the delivery ward on their own unwashed hands. He had the numbers. The wards where staff washed buried a fraction of the mothers. The profession's response was to mock him, freeze him out, and keep the gloves off, and the mothers kept dying for another two decades. Being right was not the same as being believed, and the whole gap between the two is where this deck lives.

MedKayfab: The Epistemia Edge puts the scientific method itself into the ring, every study design, every statistic, and every way a clean-looking result can quietly lie. You stop trusting a conclusion because it got published and start reading how it was actually made.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics), plus the multi-card Boss Battle combo unique to this deck
- S-Tier characters like Semme-the-Outcast, P-Hacker-the-Cheat, and Confound-the-Distractor

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the machinery of proof and the people who game it. You meet Semme-the-Outcast, the physician whose handwashing data was correct and whose colleagues let patients die rather than admit it. You meet P-Hacker-the-Cheat, who tortures a dataset until some p-value confesses to a finding that was never there, and Confound-the-Distractor, the hidden third variable that quietly takes the credit for a relationship it never caused. Correlation-the-Friend keeps insisting he is really causation, and Null-the-Boring-Ghost is the result nobody bothers to publish, which is exactly how a whole literature ends up lying by omission.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for high-stress retrieval: the Character (the concept), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the numbers that matter), the Lore (how it fools people), and the Quest (the appraisal challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is brutal here. If you cannot say in one sentence why a study is rigged or sound without looking, the claim goes through unchallenged and the "patient" on the Stage inherits whatever weak evidence you waved past. The Boss Battles chain several cards into one combo, so you have to catch the flawed design, the statistic dressing it up, and the reviewer who let it pass, all in the same round.

Honest cognitive load
This is a meta-deck, so it earns its keep next to clinical material rather than replacing it. It is built for medical students learning to read papers instead of memorizing them, residents prepping for journal club, and science communicators who keep losing the argument to a confident graph. It pairs naturally with The Differential Engine for the reasoning side and with Laboratory Medicine for the numbers, and it quietly sharpens every other MedKayfab deck, because once you can appraise a claim you stop taking anyone's facts on faith.
